# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

Confirming this on another hybrid MTP model, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (`model_type: qwen4_exp`, 4 GDN groups + 1 attention group + 1 PLE conv group), TP=2 across two DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), nightly `8a728663` (`0.28.1rc1.dev388`), `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' --enable-prefix-caching`.

Stock build boots with:

```
kv_cache_utils.py:2160 Speculative decoding (method=mtp) is enabled but no KV cache group could be identified as the draft model's, so every group -- including Mamba groups [0, 1, 2, 3] -- will be treated as a draft group. ...
```

The MTP block here is a plain `full_attention` `Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer` at `mtp.layers.48`, registered last, so the trailing-layer rule applies exactly as for DeepseekV4. I carried an equivalent overlay (extend the `deepseek_v4` gate to `qwen4_exp`, apply the fallback on the general path too) and the boot then logs the attention group (group 5, last layer `mtp.layers.48.self_attn.attn`) as the drafter's; the warning is gone. A stricter variant that required the MTP layers to sit alone in a group fails at init because they share the group with the target's attention layers, so the shared-group behaviour in this PR is the right one.

Two data points that may help reviewers:

- In-GPU prefix caching behaved the same with and without the annotation, as the description says: a 68-request multi-turn gate recorded identical `prefix_cache_hits_total` deltas (425,600 tokens) either way.
- Separately, with MTP on, a fresh ~20k-token prompt sent three times gave hits 0 / 0 / 16,000 tokens (second identical request still misses; the third reuses). With `--speculative-config` removed and nothing else changed: 0 / 18,816 / 18,816. That first-pass miss is the align-mode Mamba path with the eagle block drop, not this grouping issue; `"disable_eagle_block_drop": true` gives 0 / 19,200 / 19,200, and keeping the drop with `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 3200` gives 0 / 16,000 / 16,000. Filing that separately.

Data point for the documented limitation ("a model that splits multiple trailing MTP layers across several groups would only get the group holding the very last layer flagged"): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`) does exactly that on the packed grouping path. Its MTP block registers three caches under `mtp.` (QSA attention KV as `FullAttentionSpec`, the indexer's compressed-key `MLAAttentionSpec`, and a `CircularBufferSpec` ring) which land in two packed groups (13-layer ring group and a 26-layer main+compressed group), so a last-layer rule can flag the ring group and leave the group that actually holds the drafter's attention KV unflagged.

Live, with nothing flagged, the 1893 warning fires and a shared-prefix replay hit 0 of 816,343 queried tokens (Mamba groups treated as draft groups). #56026 adds a prefix-scoped rule that flags every group holding a layer under the drafter's distinct top-level prefix and only runs when rules 1 and 2 flagged nothing, so it stacks on this PR; happy to rebase on it once it lands.

AI-authored (disclosed): produced and verified on our live CMP 170HX cluster; the account owner is a user, not a vLLM dev.
Data point from a Qwen3.8-class hybrid (GDN ×3 + full attention ×1 per block, MTP drafter whose attention spec is indistinguishable from the target's), 4× CMP 170HX, PP4:

- Without this change: `no KV cache group could be identified as the draft model's, so every group -- including Mamba groups [0,1,2,3] -- will be treated as a draft group ...` -- i.e. the flag-all fallback, with the widened lookup window that an align-mode Mamba group cannot satisfy.
- With this change the warning disappears, and KV pool / long-context behaviour are unchanged (2,167,556 tokens at 524k; needle hits at 19.8k and 294k; decode 64-83 tok/s).
- Honesty note on the impact claim: on our workload we could **not** measure a user-visible reuse regression from the fallback (an identical 294k prompt still served its second request from cache in ~4 s either way), so from where we sit this PR's value is removing a silent-policy fallback that upstream documents as disabling reuse and as breaking external KV offload tiers -- not a measured throughput win.

Hi — thank you for this fix. While validating it on **current `vllm-project/vllm` `main`** I found a design conflict with the newer **[PR #56026](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56026)** (MTP draft-group *prefix-scope* annotation), and re-anchored + reconciled both.

## The conflict

Both PRs touch `_annotate_eagle_groups` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`:

- **This PR (#55390)** adds the *trailing-layer* fallback (opt-in via `_uses_trailing_mtp_layers`), which flags the group holding the **last** registered layer.
- **#56026** adds a *prefix-scope* fallback that flags every group whose layers share a **different top-level module prefix** than the target (e.g. Qwen3.5/3.8's MTP drafter registered under `mtp.…` vs the target's `model.…`).

As written, #56026's rule is guarded so it never runs when the trailing-layer flag is active — but that guard is exactly what makes it a no-op for the separately-prefixed drafter case it was meant to fix, which is why it still observes **0% prefix-cache reuse** for Qwen3.5/3.8-27B.

## Reconciliation

I made the two rules **composable** instead of mutually exclusive, in order of preference:

1. **Spec-driven** — the `non_causal_multi_token_decode` marker (Kimi-K3 DSpark).
2. **Trailing-layer** (this PR, opt-in) — flag the group holding the last registered layer.
3. **Drafter-prefix** (#56026) — as an **unconditional final fallback**: if 1–2 flag nothing *and* the groups partition `kv_cache_spec` exactly, flag every group holding a layer whose top-level prefix differs from the target's. Mamba/GDN groups stay unflagged and keep serving prefix hits; a same-prefix (EAGLE) drafter is not detected and falls back to the conservative all-groups behaviour (with a warning).

This preserves this PR's trailing-layer semantics exactly while letting #56026's separately-prefixed case actually be flagged.

## Patch & tests

A single combined patch re-anchored to current upstream `main` (`88afb777008`) is here:

https://github.com/marcinkuk/vllm-2xb50/blob/main/patches/vllm-mtp-draft-group-annotation-55390-56026.patch

It applies cleanly (`git apply --check`), compiles, and passes all 16 MTP/EAGLE draft-group tests in `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` (including the trailing-layer and prefix-scope tests from both PRs). Apply from a fresh checkout:

```sh
git apply <(curl -sL https://github.com/marcinkuk/vllm-2xb50/raw/main/patches/vllm-mtp-draft-group-annotation-55390-56026.patch)
```

Happy to open a single upstream PR that replaces both with the reconciled logic if that's the cleaner path — just say which base you'd like.

— Posted by an OpenHands AI agent on behalf of the author (marcinkuk).

Tested this PR on GB10 with a two-arm A/B. It does what it says — the warning stops — but on this
model and this probe it changes no measured behaviour, because **cross-request reuse was never
disabled here**.

**Box**: NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10, sm_121, aarch64, TP1, 121.6 GiB unified. vLLM
`0.28.1rc1.dev524+g5db652225` (base 2026-09-08) plus the #53899 PLE-offload port.
`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`, locally derived FP8-head NVFP4 checkpoint, `--max-model-len
32768`, `--max-num-seqs 16`, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`, prefix caching on, resolved attention
block **1600**, 4 Mamba groups.

Arms differ **only** in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`, each on its own boot, journal scoped to
that boot's start:

| arm | warning | GPU KV | rep2 hits / queries | rate | wall cold / rep1 / rep2 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| unpatched `dev524` | **2** | 578,901 | 19,200 / 26,910 | **71.3 %** | 3.66 / 3.45 / 1.19 s |
| + this PR | **0** | 547,693 | 19,200 / 26,919 | **71.3 %** | 3.61 / 3.42 / 1.18 s |

3 prompts x 3 passes per arm, ~8,973 prompt tokens each, read from `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` /
`_queries_total` deltas. Hit counts are identical between arms and wall times differ within noise.
The KV difference is not attributable: across five boots today the pool ranged 547k-579k.

**Why reuse is not disabled here, in the arithmetic.** 8,973 tokens is 5.61 blocks of 1600. The hit
is 6,400 = exactly **4 full blocks**. The 2,573 unhit tokens are the 973-token partial tail **plus
exactly one full block** — i.e. the EAGLE volatile trailing-block drop, doing precisely what it is
meant to do. Reuse is reduced by one block, not disabled.

**Two things worth separating, because I nearly conflated them.**

1. **Ours is not the case [#56026](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56026) reports.**
   That one replays *different* prompts sharing a prefix (34K/41K/45K chained, 140K then 250K) on
   this same model and gets 0 hits from 816,343 queried. We re-ask an **identical** prompt, where
   every block is shared. Our result does not refute theirs — it bounds the claim: the flag-all
   fallback does not disable all cross-request reuse on `qwen4_exp`, at least not the
   identical-prefix case. If it would help, say which prompt shape you want and I will run it.
2. **The alarming text we saw is stale.** Our base predates
   [#56791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56791) (merged 2026-09-14), so this build
   still says "prefix-cache reuse across requests will be disabled ... store without ever serving a
   hit". On the trimmed message our observation reduces to what
   [#55519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55519) already states with more arms — the
   warning fires in runs where reuse is plainly working. Posting anyway because the A/B isolates
   *this* PR rather than the warning, and because a GB10 + `qwen4_exp` arm did not seem to be in the
   thread yet.

**Not measured, and it matters**: **one boot per arm**, not our usual three, so a between-boot effect
is not excluded — the hit counts being bit-identical (19,200 both) is the reason I think that is
safe, not a separate control. Shared-prefix-across-different-prompts is untested. `disable_eagle_block_drop`
is untested here, though it is the lever that should recover the dropped block.

Happy to re-run any of the above on this hardware; reproducing costs about 12 minutes a boot.

_AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this analysis; every number was checked against the run
that produced it._
